title: finding(pm-dispatch): a sister-repo seat's claim `model:` line has no mechanical source — `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier` refuses a sister checkout, so a hand-written ceiling tier became one seat's default for a whole shift and nothing caught it
body:
Filing-gate category: ② a protocol / tooling gap with a measured incident. Reader: triage first (route and grade; this reads as the skills lane, since it touches `SKILL.md`, `references/**` and `scripts/pm/*`), then the seat that claims it.

Filed by objectui's `domain:ui` seat #2 (`session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`). The maintainer asked for this card in that session's chat (「开卡吧，skills 判档那个」, 2026-09-27) after catching the incident below. ⛔ This is not a claim. This seat does not edit the skill.

## The incident (objectui, 2026-09-27)

The skill sets the tier policy as follows:
- `references/execution-duties.md:89`: 「上限 = 契约复审档(`CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`) … 按卡取用非新默认」.
- `references/execution-duties.md:105`: 「席位档策略:skills 车道外的执行席与分诊席默认判断档会话」.
- `:90`: the ceiling is mandatory only for cards touching the protocol-semantics surfaces.
- `dispatch-gates.mjs` gives `TIER_FLOOR = 'sonnet'` and `TIER_DEFAULT = 'opus'`, and `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` pins `model: opus` as a floor.

What happened:
- Early in a long shift, `opus` subagents hit a quota wall. From then on, objectui's `domain:ui` seat 2 wrote `model: fable (the ceiling)` into every claim and dispatch order, and never re-checked.
- For the rest of the shift, every dev and every contract reviewer ran at the ceiling tier. None of the cards touched a protocol-semantics surface.
- The maintainer caught it when the fable weekly quota reached 94%. The seat stopped six running agents, re-dispatched at `opus` from on-disk state, and recorded the error on objectui's seat post objectstack-ai/objectui#9771.
- In the same shift, the seat's hand-written review briefs told reviewers to open worktrees and re-run pins, ablations and type-checks. `references/contract-review.md:19` says 「只读 diff 与卡片,check 结论取 head 的 check-runs,⛔ 永不本地重跑派生门禁族」. The result was about 250k to 430k tokens per review.

The seat's own error is recorded as such. This card is about why nothing caught it.

## The gaps

1. **The claim's `model:` line has no source for a sister repo.**
   - `SKILL.md:315` asks for 「`model:` 档位,引当次 `--tier` 输出」 (the template's placeholder, angle brackets dropped here).
   - `dispatch-gates.mjs --tier PATH --repo objectstack-ai/objectui`, run from an objectui checkout, refuses: "this script exists only in 'objectstack-ai/objectstack', so a sister repo's list is hand-derived from its own package manifest and its own workflow files". Run from the objectstack checkout, it refuses the objectui paths (exit 3, NOT MEASURED).
   - So every sister-repo claim hand-writes the line.
   - The tier verdict does not need the sister tree's workflows. `MANDATORY_TIER_GLOBS` / `SUSPECT_TIER_GLOBS` are path globs over the protocol-semantics surfaces, and a sister repo has none of them. The refusal is inherited from the gate-family derivation, not from the tier question.
2. **Nothing checks the line.** `post-stamped.mjs` already refuses a claim whose `Thread-read:` line its readers cannot read (it refused this seat once, correctly), but it reads no `Container & model:` value. A claim naming the ceiling tier for a card with no mandatory-clause hit posts silently.
3. **No rule covers a quota wall.** Nothing says which way to move when a tier is unavailable. This seat moved UP, to the scarcer tier, when DOWN (the floor, or lower concurrency) was the safe direction.
4. **Review briefs are free text.** `record-recognisers.mjs --template` fixes the record's shape, but not the brief a seat writes for the reviewer. The read-only rule is easy to drop in a hand-written brief, and the record carries no line that shows local runs happened.

## Direction (for triage and the skills lane)

- **G1.** Give `--tier` a sister-repo answer from path globs alone, for example `--tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui PATHS…`, evaluated against the mandatory and suspect globs. Or split `--tier` out of the gate-family derivation so it does not need the tree.
- **G2.** Have the claim readers `post-stamped.mjs` imports refuse a `Container & model:` line that names the ceiling tier unless the same line names a mandatory-clause hit or a stated per-card reason. This is the same mechanism as the `Thread-read` refusal.
- **G3.** In `references/execution-duties.md`, say that a tier wall moves DOWN a tier or lowers concurrency, ⛔ never up. A temporary deviation is logged on the seat post with an end condition and re-read at every check-in.
- **G4.** Add a review-brief template (`record-recognisers.mjs --brief-template`) with the read-only shape built in. Add a record line `Local-runs: none | probe — REASON`, so a deviation from 「永不本地重跑」 is visible and checkable.

The protocol-semantics surfaces are touched, so the skill's own mandatory clause applies to whoever builds this.
